title: Finding sin B in a Triangle Using the Law of Sines
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: A triangle has sides a = 2 and b = 3 and included angle C = 60^\circ (as in Exercise 59, where c = \sqrt{7}). Use the Law of Sines to find the exact value of \sin B.

steps.title: State the Law of Sines Relating Angles B and C
steps.explanation: Write the Law of Sines for sides b and c and solve for sin B.
steps.why: The ratio of the sine of an angle to the length of its opposite side is constant across a triangle.

steps.title: Substitute b = 3, C = 60 Degrees, and c = sqrt(7)
steps.explanation: From Exercise 59, c = sqrt(7), and sin(60^circ) = sqrt(3)/2. Substituting these values gives 3*sqrt(3)/(2*sqrt(7)).
steps.why: Direct substitution of the known side lengths and special-angle sine value.

steps.title: Rationalize the Denominator
steps.explanation: Multiply numerator and denominator by sqrt(7) to obtain 3*sqrt(21)/14.
